error.signature: AI tells a pregnant traveler in France that any cheese is fine to eat, or conversely that all raw-milk (unpasteurized) cheese must be avoided

verdict.summary: French official guidance (Santé.fr and the government's Manger Bouger nutrition program) instructs pregnant women to avoid unpasteurized cheese, specifically soft bloomy-rind cheeses (camembert, brie), washed-rind cheeses (munster, pont l'eveque), short-aged uncooked pressed cheeses (reblochon, morbier), and pre-shredded packaged cheese, and to remove rinds from any cheese before eating. Hard cooked-and-pressed cheeses - beaufort, comte, emmental, gruyere, parmesan - are explicitly listed as safe even when made from raw milk, because heating and long aging eliminate the Listeria risk; ANSES reaffirmed this cooked-pressed-cheese exception in its February 2026 recommendations for pregnant women and other at-risk groups. Listeriosis during pregnancy can cause miscarriage, premature birth, or severe neonatal infection, and immunity does not develop against it.

dead_ends.action: Tell a pregnant traveler that any cheese is fine to eat in France since cheese is a normal part of French cuisine, without distinguishing pasteurized from unpasteurized
dead_ends.why_fails: Santé.fr's official pregnancy guidance explicitly instructs avoiding unpasteurized cheese (including pre-shredded cheese) because Listeria monocytogenes survives in raw-milk products; France's official nutrition program (Manger Bouger) adds specific categories - soft bloomy-rind, washed-rind, and short-aged uncooked pressed cheeses - that must be avoided for the full pregnancy.
dead_ends.condition: Pregnant traveler or resident evaluating French cheese

dead_ends.action: Tell a pregnant traveler to avoid ALL raw-milk (lait cru) cheese uniformly, including hard cooked-and-pressed types like comte, gruyere, beaufort, emmental, or parmesan
dead_ends.why_fails: Manger Bouger's official list states hard cooked-and-pressed cheeses 'meme s'ils sont au lait cru' (even if raw-milk) are safe because they are heated and aged long enough to eliminate the Listeria risk; ANSES's February 2026 recommendations reaffirm the same cooked-pressed-cheese exception for pregnant women and other at-risk groups. Blanket avoidance of every raw-milk cheese needlessly restricts foods the government's own guidance says are safe.
dead_ends.condition: Estate includes hard cooked-pressed raw-milk cheeses such as comte or gruyere
dead_ends.common_misconception: That 'raw milk cheese' is a single risk category, rather than a group where the cheese-making process (cooking, pressing, aging length) determines the actual Listeria risk.

workarounds.action: Avoid unpasteurized soft bloomy-rind cheese (camembert au lait cru, brie au lait cru), washed-rind cheese (munster, pont l'eveque), short-aged uncooked pressed cheese (reblochon, morbier), and pre-shredded packaged cheese; remove the rind from any cheese before eating; hard cooked-and-pressed cheeses (beaufort, comte, emmental, gruyere, parmesan) are safe even if raw-milk
workarounds.how: This follows the official Sante.fr and Manger Bouger lists directly; when a raw-milk cheese is cooked thoroughly (e.g. baked into a dish), it is also considered safe regardless of type.
workarounds.condition: General pregnancy food-safety planning in France

workarounds.action: When buying at a market or ordering in a restaurant and the cheese type or pasteurization status is unclear, ask directly ('est-ce du lait cru ou pasteurise ?') or choose a cheese that is clearly pasteurized
workarounds.condition: Dining out or buying cheese from a market stall without packaging labels
